java.finding: Factories are tried in fixed order and the first factory that consumes the complete source wins: Sequence, Class, Activity, Description, then State among the relevant candidates.
The end-anchored message grammar accepts ordinary identifier endpoints, including Node, Component, and Queue, and implicitly creates participants.
Explicit class/object declarations, package containers, and class links remain owned by the earlier Class factory when every command is consumable.
Component, deployment, use-case, and Archimate command competitors share one later Description factory.

rust.finding: detect_uml_subtype approximates complete-factory consumption with scores and local booleans.

Lines whose first token is Node or Queue receive Deployment declaration score, and a line beginning Component plus whitespace receives Component declaration score, before establishing that the complete line is a relationship command.

f0ffaa30's looks_like_mixed_leaf_declaration correctly stops reserved-word relationship endpoints from rejecting a viable Class candidate, but it does not protect the Sequence-first relationship-only case from Deployment/Component scoring.
Generic other_max + 1 adjustments encode earlier-factory precedence for selected cases, but no whole-source command-consumption model prevents the reserved-endpoint false declaration.
